name: Input capture
threading: One audio thread calls process() (no allocation, locks or I/O); every other call is a message or worker thread. State changes hand the buffer between the threads with release/acquire stores, so no locks exist.
standalone_test_command: cmake -S modules/input_capture -B build/input_capture && cmake --build build/input_capture && ctest --test-dir build/input_capture
summary: Records the track's audio input into a preallocated buffer, either free-running (a ring that keeps the last N seconds) or synced to the host's bar grid (starts on the next bar line, ends by ppq so tempo changes stay bar-exact). Four states (Idle, Armed, Capturing, Captured), sample-accurate start, meters with clip counting, and an O(frames) hand-off of the planar audio.
public_api: `CaptureEngine::process(in, numChannels, frames, CaptureTransport)` (audio thread) and `onPrepare(sampleRate, channels)`
limits: Mono or stereo, 8 kHz to 384 kHz, at most 60 s, 100 MiB and 11,520,000 frames; memory is allocated per arm and released when the capture ends, so an idle engine holds nothing
adapters: Call process() from the host's audio callback before anything that overwrites the input buffer, forward the transport (playing, ppq, bpm), and run take() on a worker thread.
adapter_notes: The engine never touches a file or the project; the caller turns CapturedAudio into its own source type.
removal: Delete the folder; callers lose input capture only.
